items.heading: ## Custom REST Endpoints and CXF
items.text: The platform does not provide Server-Sent Events. No SSE classes or `text/event-stream` handling exist in the JUDO sources, and the Karaf features install only the upstream `cxf-jaxrs` feature (Apache CXF 3.6.8). An SSE endpoint needs a CXF SSE module that the platform does not install.

items.heading: ### File-Store Servlet Checks
items.text:
- `DownloadServlet` has no size limit setting; only `UploadServlet` has `maxSize`.
- Every file the generated frontend downloads comes through the app's `download` path (`/<app>/download`, served by `DownloadServlet`). An operation's `downloadToken` is redeemed on that path.
items.replaces: - `DownloadServlet` has no size limit setting; only `UploadServlet` has `maxSize`.

items.heading: Optimistic Locking and `__version`
items.text: - The generated TypeScript REST client copies `__version` only when its runtime type is `string`, but the generated `JudoStored` type declares it as `number`, so a UI built on that client drops the version on update. Send `__version` explicitly in the update payload until the generator copies numbers.

items.heading: ### Default Values on Type Creation
items.text: The seeded string types in the platform test fixture models are `String` (`maxLength` 255), `Text` (250), `Phone` (20), `URL` (1024) and `Email` (255, with an email `regExp`). A new model may change them, so check its own types before relying on these limits.
items.replaces: *Verify:* the seeded string and numeric types of a new model (names, `maxLength`, `regExp`) against the project template before documenting them.

items.heading: ### Rules for `accesses[*].getterExpression`
items.text: 4. **`<Type>!getVariable(...)` returns a scalar `String` only.** The receiver must be a type name (for example `String!getVariable('ACTOR', 'email')`); a bare `!getVariable(...)` is not a valid form. The type must be a primitive, enumeration or custom type, otherwise the build fails with `Type is not valid for environment variable`.

items.heading: Attribute-less singleton: initializer and application container
items.text: The platform calls every initializer operation (unbound, no parameters) at each start of the application, after the persistence, scripts, SDK operations and identity-manager services are ready. The startup code calls each one with an empty exchange map and sets no principal.
items.replaces: The platform calls every initializer operation (unbound, no parameters) at each start of the application, once the scripts are ready.

items.heading: Shape of the Generated Tree
items.text: - A node with no children is emitted as a leaf that carries only `id` and `label` (binary inputs and filters get their extra keys). A container, table or tab element without children therefore has no `_id`, `_label` or `tab` entries.

items.heading: Backend guidance
items.text: A JCL script operation cannot raise a modeled fault and cannot call an OSGi service. The JCL grammar has no `throw` or fault statement and no service-reference form; its statements are declarations, calls, `return`, `unset`, `delete`, `new`, blocks, `if`, `for` and `while`. Put fault-raising logic and OSGi service calls in a Java custom implementation.

items.heading: When No Manual Step Is Needed
items.text: At startup, the database prehook logs `ERROR ... Could not find compatible schema model` when the database already holds a stored model version that the built model does not match, after its retry attempts. It is a startup log, not a build failure: run the schema upgrade for that database (see the migration rules below).
